officialTitle: Tucatinib, Trastuzumab, and Capecitabine for HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer
setting: Previously treated metastatic (after trastuzumab, pertuzumab and T-DM1)

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Secondary end points, assessed in the total population (612 patients), included overall survival, progression-free survival among patients with brain metastases, confirmed objective response rate, and safety.
secondaryEndpoints: PFS in patients with brain metastases
design.notes: Patients with or without brain metastases were eligible.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding the HER2-selective TKI tucatinib to trastuzumab and capecitabine improve outcomes in heavily pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, including patients with brain metastases?

pico.population: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab, pertuzumab and trastuzumab emtansine, with or without brain metastases
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS (first 480 patients). Secondary: OS, PFS in brain metastases, confirmed ORR, safety

publications.title: Tucatinib, Trastuzumab, and Capecitabine for HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Progression-free survival at 1 year was 33.1% in the tucatinib-combination group and 12.3% in the placebo-combination group (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.71; P<0.001), and the median duration of progression-free survival was 7.8 months and 5.6 months, respectively.

Overall survival at 2 years was 44.9% in the tucatinib-combination group and 26.6% in the placebo-combination group (hazard ratio for death, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.88; P = 0.005), and the median overall survival was 21.9 months and 17.4 months, respectively.

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS in patients with brain metastases
outcomes.sourceQuote: Among the patients with brain metastases, progression-free survival at 1 year was 24.9% in the tucatinib-combination group and 0% in the placebo-combination group (hazard ratio, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.34 to 0.69; P<0.001), and the median progression-free survival was 7.6 months and 5.4 months, respectively.

safety.description: Grade 3 or higher diarrhoea and elevated aminotransferases more common with tucatinib
safety.sourceQuote: Common adverse events in the tucatinib group included diarrhea, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome, nausea, fatigue, and vomiting. Diarrhea and elevated aminotransferase levels of grade 3 or higher were more common in the tucatinib-combination group than in the placebo-combination group.

strengths: Deliberately included patients with brain metastases, a population often excluded from trials
OS benefit observed as a secondary endpoint
limitations: Population pretreated with trastuzumab, pertuzumab and T-DM1; sequencing relative to trastuzumab deruxtecan not addressed
Primary endpoint assessed in a subset (first 480 patients)

clinicalImplications.text: Supports tucatinib plus trastuzumab and capecitabine for pretreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, with particular relevance for patients with brain metastases.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Brain metastases did not exclude patients in HER2CLIMB — consider this regimen when intracranial control is a priority.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 31825569.
